summaries.headline: Blood sugar spikes could hinge on the order you eat
bullets: A simple change to the order in which you eat could help blunt blood sugar spikes, new research suggests, but experts say it's not necessarily a "quick fix." In a study published in the journal Diabetes in October, mice that received olive oil 15 minutes before glucose — a simple sugar the body uses for energy — had a smaller early rise in blood sugar than mice given glucose first or glucose alone.
The researchers also saw the effect in mice with type 2 diabetes and severe insulin deficiency.
